analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Moving Deliberately
key_insights: A week of central bank decisions showed a deliberate approach to further tightening, leaving risk asset volatility as the main driver of global duration. AI-related worries have replaced energy risks as the primary driver of rates.
GS estimates real money is still underweight duration and sees room for the rally to extend if risk asset volatility persists.

GS closes its receive 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly and adds a long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly (entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp). Reasons: less very front-end hike risk, 5s tend to outperform during and right after hiking cycles, and the skew of long-end risks at next week's refunding.

Fed: the FOMC statement and Chair Warsh's press conference reinforced GS economists' every-other-meeting view of hikes. Baseline is one more hike in December, with a risk of a third hike in March if inflation surprises up.

Warsh said the Fed will devote one meeting next year and two in 2028 to broad policy strategy. The curve steepened on this, read as dovish. GS would be surprised if it constrained the Fed's ability to act when the case is clear.

Next week's midterm elections will affect rates mainly through perceived implications for AI and developments in the Iran conflict. A weaker risk tone makes the market more prone to react to a downside surprise in next Friday's labor report.

Treasury refunding: GS expects 10-to-30y coupon auction sizes unchanged and buyback sizes maintained or modestly increased. A cut to long-end sizes is a risk but not the base case. GS expects guidance to signal future adjustments and increases to 2-to-7y sizes starting May 2027.

Long-end spreads remain wide to fair value and longer-term forwards are only modestly above fair value. Pressure has been at the very front end, where T-bills have cheapened versus OIS since late August on elevated bill supply, money funds shortening maturity, and zero money fund AUM growth since summer.
Market expectations lean toward reduced long-end auction sizes, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve. GS expects the impact to be contained.

BoC raised rates 25bp as expected with a more hawkish tone but guided to proceeding carefully. Markets price 13bp of hikes by year-end and about 100bp through end-2027. GS sees CAD front-end hike premium as excessive and favors 1y1y vs 1y or CORH7Z7 flatteners (entry 40bp, target 25bp, stop 50bp).

GS's three reasons for the BoC view: trim and median inflation are below 2%, GS economists expect year-end 2027 inflation 40bp below the BoC's estimate, AI volatility has weighed on peers' hike pricing, and upside data would pull hikes forward rather than raise the cumulative amount.

ECB is on track for a December hike. Lagarde's communication pointed to a high bar not to hike, so the market should decay toward fully pricing it. The restrained tone on sovereign spreads should dampen volatility.

GS sees risks skewed toward 5y outperformance on the EUR curve, citing the link between 5s and rate vol, elevated EUR rate vol versus fair value, and TTF prices near the commodities team's upside scenario. Energy uncertainty supports a flatter 2s5s.

EU bonds look roughly fair against the EGB complex, trading in line with euro area aggregate fundamentals rather than their AAA rating. GS sees EU outperformance risk in 2027 because NGEU issuance ends in 2026 and EU issuance roughly halves to €70bn.

BoE is expected to deliver its first hike of the cycle next week, with one more in February. With substantial tightening already priced, the bar to out-hawk front-end pricing is high. Energy escalation is the main risk, and in that case the UK front end would underperform Europe.

GBP-EUR front-end vol differential has compressed well below what the rates differential implies. GS sees the balance tilted to long GBP versus EUR front-end vol, with owning front-end GBP receivers versus EUR as the expression, most likely paying off on energy de-escalation.

UK Autumn Budget broadly matched expectations: deficit path revised £13bn higher per year on average, headroom fell to £15bn, and the gilt remit rose only £4bn with the long-term share cut from about 10% to 6%. GS prefers Gilts versus swaps, sees modest further long-end swap spread widening, and expects 10y gilts to underperform peers because fiscal problems are unresolved. Gross gilt supply is expected above £300bn in 2027/28.

BoJ: GS economists moved their expected next hike to December on Ueda's comments on price upside risks, caution about yen weakness from foreign hikes, and receding fiscal concerns. Safe-haven demand and AI concerns have driven JGB curve flattening and long-end outperformance, and GS expects that to continue if risk-off persists.

RBNZ held the OCR in a 4-3 split vote despite a largely priced hike, citing an inflation undershoot and lower energy passthrough. GS economists now expect hikes in December and March, below market pricing. GS favors 2s10s NZD steepeners (entry 61bp, target 75bp, stop 54bp) as NZD term premium is the lowest among peers.

RBA is expected to hike next week, which GS economists expect to be the last of the cycle. GS keeps a preference for AUD front-end flattening such as 2s5s and closes its IRZ6U7 flattener for potential profit of 25bp on unclear asymmetry around the meeting.

risk_factors: Energy escalation, including the Iran conflict, could hurt UK and European front-end rates.
AI-related risk asset volatility could reverse or extend the duration rally.
A Treasury refunding that cuts long-end sizes, or leaves them unchanged against expectations of a cut, could move the long-end spread curve.
US inflation upside surprise could bring a third Fed hike in March.
A French rating downgrade and sovereign spread widening in the euro area.
Unresolved UK fiscal challenges and higher gilt issuance in 2027/28 and 2028/29.
A weak US labor report next Friday in a weaker risk tone could cause a larger market reaction.
A Fed hike widening rate differentials could weaken the yen.

Exhibit 2 shows money market fund AUM growth has stalled since summer.
Exhibit 3 shows near-term CAD forwards bore the brunt of the March to October energy-shock selloff and have seen little relief month-to-date.
Exhibit 6 shows the GBP-EUR 1y1y front-end implied vol differential has diverged from the 1y1y OIS rate differential.
Exhibit 7 shows projected gross gilt issuance revised higher for 2027/28 and 2028/29 versus the March OBR forecast.
vol_and_positioning: AI-related volatility has taken over from energy prices as the driver of 10y UST yield moves (Exhibit 1 correlations).
Euro rates vol is elevated versus GS's fair value model. TTF prices are close to the commodities team's upside scenario.
GBP-EUR 1y1y front-end implied vol differential is well below what the rates differential would imply. GS prefers long GBP versus EUR front-end vol.
GS Option implied position indicator reads 0, Fund Positioning Indicator reads -3, and Data Response Indicator reads -1 (GS says real money is underweight duration).
CFTC duration-weighted positioning: Spec net short in all listed contracts including SFR at -74.5 and TY at -56.8 $mm/bp; Asset managers net long in TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN.
geopolitical: Iran conflict developments are cited as a driver of rates alongside AI volatility after next week's midterm elections.
Energy escalation is a risk to UK front-end pricing and to the ECB path.
Risk of French sovereign rating downgrade and its spillover to OAT and BTP spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects unchanged 10-to-30y auction sizes, with a modest buyback increase and guidance toward more 2-to-7y supply from May 2027, a contained impact on long-end spreads.
tension_points.bear_case: Market expectations lean toward reduced long-end sizes, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut to long-end auction sizes at next week's refunding announcement would invalidate GS's base case.

tension_points.bull_case: BoC hawkish tone and energy upside risk could justify more hikes, with a December hike possible on an inflation surprise or trade deal.
tension_points.bear_case: Trim and median inflation are below 2%, growth is below potential, and AI volatility weighs on peers' hike pricing, so GS sees the premium as excessive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A December hike following a meaningful upside inflation surprise or a trade deal.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth, a firmer labor market and energy pressure support the BoE's hiking path.
tension_points.bear_case: With substantial tightening already priced, the bar for more front-end cheapening is high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed energy pressures or an adverse energy scenario would push the UK front end to underperform.
